issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a public SealSaloon(String) constructor that takes the saloon name, but both the provided example in Main and the solution implement/use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This discrepancy will confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether they must store a saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent: either change the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument SealSaloon() constructor or update the template Main and the solution to call new SealSaloon(String) and add a private final String name field (with a getter) to SealSaloon. Also update any example code and tests to use the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs that both attributes (orders and stock) should be initialized to default values in the SealSaloon constructor, but it also requires the stock attribute to be static and final (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is inconsistent/incorrect. The solution initializes the static final stock at field declaration instead, which differs from the text guidance and may confuse students.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the initialization instructions: specify that orders (an instance field) should be initialized in the constructor, while the shared static final stock should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or reword the sentence that says both should be initialized in the constructor to avoid encouraging students to assign a static final field inside an instance constructor.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but the provided solution implements a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and the template's Main usage also instantiates SealSaloon with no arguments. This creates an API mismatch between the described requirement and the actual code students will see, causing confusion about the expected constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent: either update the solution and template to provide a constructor matching the problem (public SealSaloon(String name) that initializes fields and optionally stores the name) or modify the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument constructor. Ensure examples in Main and the UML match the implemented API.
